chapter: Louis Armstrong, Gene Krupa and the drum school
title: The Metropole and Red Allen

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, that was a very funny place, wasn't it?
The Metropole?
Yeah.

Well after you got there, after you played there for a while, you'd have to play in there for a while to get used to it, because you were spread out behind the bar. But after you got accustomed to it, it was all right, you got used to the sound. And it was a fun place to work. It was hard work. But it was a fun place to work. And I remember some beautiful times in there with Red Allen, Charlie Shavers, Roy, just everybody worked there.
Coleman Hawkins.
Hawkins, that's right, and Sol Yaged and everybody working there, Woody Herman with a small band, with a big band.
How about Hamp?

Hamp with a big band, that's right, Gene Krupa, Diz, Adderley--Cannonball, him and Nat Adderley, and so you remember some awful nice times working in there, in the Metropole. Well the one who really built that Metropole was Henry Red Allen. He had a number he used to do, 'Kiss the Baby.' People used to come from all over the world if they had a new date, to come in and holler up at Red, 'play 'Kiss the Baby.' And they'd play 'Kiss the Baby.'
Here's someone we really hadn't touched on.
You knew him 20 odd years before, right?
Who's that, Red?
Yah.
Oh Red Allen, he's the one that built the Metropole. He was with Lynn Russell for a long while and a great trumpet player.
Oh yeah.

Could sing and entertain and just a grand guy. Everybody loved Red. Henry Red Allen. Buster Bailey, another great artist. But Henry Red Allen, he is the one that really built that Metropole, because of all of us helped, but Red was the main man there.
And he was there for years, right?
Oh yeah, yeah. Henry Red Allen. Made a lot of records with him, too. Under his name.
Who was on 'Ride Red Ride,' was that you?
I made 'Ride Red Ride,' but the first 'Ride Red Ride,' I think it was Panama; they were all with Lucky Millender.
But the LP, the one with Coleman Hawkins on it and Buster Bailey.
It may have been me.
I've heard that record.
Yeah, 'Ride Red Ride,' yeah. I know I did a 'Ride Red Ride' with Red. Now the original was with Lucky
Millinder, Panama Francis was.
